findings.reason: CCN 35 is accurate, but 25 of its 34 increments are inline fallback/selection expressions within a single 31-field session record. Only three if statements and two guard returns exist; no loop or await. Existing domain operations already use named helpers. Extracting the whole literal only relocates almost all complexity; splitting grade/correction/genre fragments adds schema assembly indirection without removing a demonstrated maintenance defect. Combining repeated reads changes evaluation semantics and the genre fallbacks differ. Retain the coherent constructor and documented save ordering.

NLOC 62 is accurate. The 31-field session schema accounts for most lines; guards precede it and a short pending-state/persistence publication sequence follows it. Keeping one complete literal makes the saved schema and evaluation order inspectable in one place. Moving fields to one-use helpers or compressing formatting would reduce the reported size without a corresponding maintenance benefit. No small cohesive improvement was identified within the assigned scope.
